name: Tripeptide-29
lead: Tripeptide-29 is a small collagen-derived peptide made of glycine, proline and hydroxyproline, used in firming and anti-aging skincare. It is added to creams and serums to support the skin's look of firmness and smoothness.
It is a cosmetic ingredient. The FDA says US law does not recognize cosmeceuticals as a category [1]. Published human studies on this specific ingredient are limited.

chain: Signals skin cells that collagen is being broken down
angle.text: Used in firming creams and serums, tripeptide-29 is applied daily to improve skin firmness and fine lines.

paras: Tripeptide-29 is found in firming serums, neck creams and anti-aging moisturizers, sometimes alongside other peptides.

Matrikine-type peptides are fragments of structural proteins; suppliers say they signal skin cells to make new collagen. Another cosmetic peptide, palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (Matrixyl), is classed similarly and launched in 2000 [2].

card.summary: A collagen-fragment peptide in firming creams that people use to make skin look firmer and smoother.

quick.overview:
Tripeptide-29 is a three-amino-acid collagen fragment used in firming skincare. People apply it to help skin look firmer and smoother.

It is found in over-the-counter serums and creams.
quick.mechanism: Suppliers describe it as a signal peptide telling skin cells to make collagen, similar in concept to other matrikine peptides [2].
quick.risks: It is a cosmetic ingredient, so claims are not pre-approved [1]. Mild irritation is possible for sensitive skin.
